name: Wave D: VerifiedSTH type-state for verify-before-commit
description:
Type-state pattern: a translog.STH can ONLY be persisted into the vault
after passing VerifyAndCrossCheck. Currently this is a runtime
assertion at every call site. Make it a compile-time guarantee.

Bug pattern this eliminates: "wrong ordering" (20% of all bugs) +
"persist before verify" subset of "missing check".

## Design

```go
// internal/cli/translog.go

// VerifiedSTH proves that an STH passed full server-pub +
// inclusion + consistency + (optional) witness cross-check.
// Constructible ONLY via VerifyAndCrossCheck.
type VerifiedSTH struct {
    // private fields — no other package can construct
    sth     translog.STH
    server  CanonicalURL
    chainID ScopeID
}

func (v *VerifiedSTH) STH() translog.STH { return v.sth }
func (v *VerifiedSTH) Encode() ([]byte, error) { ... }

// Returns *VerifiedSTH only if everything verifies.
func VerifyAndCrossCheck(...) (*VerifiedSTH, error)
```

Then ScopeData.LastSTH update only via:
```go
func (sd *ScopeData) PersistLastSTH(v *VerifiedSTH) {
    sd.LastSTH, _ = v.Encode()
}
```

Calling `sd.LastSTH = encodedRawSTH` becomes a private-field violation
(or we remove the public field entirely and force going through
PersistLastSTH).

## Acceptance

- VerifiedSTH cannot be constructed outside `cli` package
- Persist functions take *VerifiedSTH, not raw STH
- A test that tries to construct VerifiedSTH externally fails to compile
  (verified by running `go build ./...` after a deliberate violation)
- All tests green

## Bug classes eliminated

- sync.go:430 "push verify proves wrong event" — caller can no longer
  hand a raw STH past verify
- "Wrong ordering: persist before verify" — compile error

## Effort

1 day. Smaller refactor than Wave C.

## Dependencies

Should land AFTER Wave C (CanonicalURL + ScopeID feed VerifiedSTH).

name: Wave F: Spec compliance test generator (optional)
description:
Optional / lower priority. Generate test stubs from PROTOCOL.md /
TRANSLOG.md / STORAGE.md / API.md MUST-clauses so spec drift fails
CI immediately.

## Background

10% of bugs found were "spec drift" — implementation didn't match the
documented behavior. Examples:
- payload_key fresh-per-save promise vs SaveBody reuse
- nil vs empty bytes for genesis prev_hash
- /users events `since` inclusivity vs API.md spec

Most spec-drift bugs are catchable via "implementation matches doc"
tests, but writing them by hand is tedious.

## Approach

Build `tools/spec-coverage/`:
1. Parse PROTOCOL.md / TRANSLOG.md / STORAGE.md / API.md.
2. Extract every MUST/SHOULD clause + its surrounding context.
3. Emit Go test stubs grouped by spec file + section.
4. Each stub has the spec quote as comment + a TODO assertion.
5. Tester fills in assertions (the WHAT comes from spec; the HOW is engineering).

CI gate: % coverage of MUSTs >= 90%.

## Acceptance

- `go run ./tools/spec-coverage/` regenerates test stubs in
  internal/spec_compliance_test.go.
- Generated stubs have spec quotes as comments.
- Coverage report: # of MUSTs in spec / # with corresponding test.
- CI fails if any generated stub is empty (TODO assertion not filled in).

## Effort

3-5 days. Markdown parsing + Go AST generation + initial fill-in of
the most security-critical assertions.

## Status

Lower priority — Waves A-E will reduce bug rate significantly already.
F is "long-tail spec drift". Reserve for v1.x.

name: Wave E: chain.Tx transactional file ops
result:

## What landed

- internal/chain/tx_test.go (new):
  - Roundtrip + rollback + idempotency + nonexistent-file cases
  - Property test: 200 random seeds, two invariants
    - I1: final size ∈ {preSize, preSize + Σ committed}
    - I2: subsequent Cleanup is no-op (no drift)

- internal/cli/sync.go: pull-loop migrated to AppendTx
  - 3 separate `rollbackTruncate()` call sites consolidated
  - `fileSize` helper deleted (was only consumer)

  impossible — Cleanup returns the truncate error.
- Forgot truncate on new error path: defer-friendly, auto-rollback

- Partial AppendRaw rollback gap (sync.go:319): closed.

## Codex review (commit 0de52b1)

"No actionable correctness issues were found in the introduced
AppendTx implementation or its migration in sync.go."

name: Wave B: Decompose cli/sync.go god-object
description:
cli/sync.go is currently ~1500 LOC and accounts for ~30% of all critical
bugs found across review rounds. This is structural: the file orchestrates
vault + chain + server + witness + translog + crypto + agent, with 5
distinct VerifyAndCrossCheck call sites each with their own rollback /
retry / commit logic.

Goal: split into focused files, each with a tight invariant set and its
own test file. Reduces per-LOC bug density without changing behavior.

## Decomposition

```
internal/cli/
├── sync.go              ← orchestrator only (RunSync, ~150 LOC)
├── sync_pull.go         ← per-scope pull processing + scope-id check + AppendRaw rollback
├── sync_push.go         ← push building + push-result verification + STH ordering guard
├── sync_reconcile.go    ← reconcile + retry budget + rebuild events
├── sync_userchain.go    ← user chain registration + push (currently inline + partial)
└── sync_internal.go     ← shared helpers (leafHashAtSeq, scopeLastSTHSize, etc.)
```

Each file gets its own _test.go with focused unit tests per phase
(complementing the existing integration suites).

## Constraints

- Pure refactor: no behavior change, no new bugs introduced.
- Every existing test must still pass at every commit.
- Keep the existing comments/security annotations intact.
- Internal-only refactor; no exported API changes.

## Acceptance

- 17 integration suites green
- Full Go test suite green
- `wc -l internal/cli/sync.go` ≤ 200 lines (was 1500+)
- `wc -l internal/cli/sync_*.go` per file ≤ 400 lines

## Bug classes mitigated

- "Wrong ordering" bugs (20%) — easier to spot in 300-LOC files
- "Missing check" bugs (40%) — code review finds gaps faster

## Effort

1 day. Pure refactor; mechanical work.

## Approach

1. Identify natural boundaries (pull/push/reconcile/userchain).
2. Move functions one-by-one, keeping the file building.
3. Test at each move.
4. Final pass: rename helpers that are now in scoped files.
result:
Decomposed cli/sync.go from 1480 → 625 LOC by extracting three new
files. Pure refactor: every function moved verbatim, every comment +
security annotation preserved, no behavioral change.

## What landed (commit fa1fed7)

- sync.go (625 LOC, was 1480): RunSync + compactAfterSync + signedPOST.
  Orchestrator + transport seam.
- sync_internal.go (175 LOC, new): shared helpers — buildSyncRequestBody,
  pushItemFor, leafHashAtSeq, scopeLastSTHSize, readAll, decryptSecretBody,
  upsertOEK, fileSize.
- sync_discover.go (149 LOC, new): discoverScope — first-time pull of
  newly admitted scopes. Translog verify BEFORE disk write, replay
  BEFORE vault commit, no half-state on any failure.
- sync_reconcile.go (607 LOC, new): divergence recovery + rebuild loop —
  reconcileAndRepush, fullPullScope, savePendingLocalEvents,
  replaceLocalChain, applyReplayedScope, rebuildAndPushSet,
  rebuildAndPushMemberChange, pushRebuiltEvent, pendingEvent type.

## Acceptance

- go build / vet / test all green
- make lint 0 issues
- 17 integration suites: 361 PASS, 0 FAIL
- sync_*.go per-file ≤ 607 LOC (originally <= 400 target — sync_reconcile
  is the unsplit divergence-recovery cluster; further split would split
  the rebuild family across files which couples worse than the size cost)

## Deviation from acceptance

The dex acceptance said `sync.go ≤ 200 LOC`. Final is 625 because
RunSync is itself ~480 LOC and was not subdivided in this wave. Further
sub-phase extraction (pull-loop, push-result-loop, conflict-retry) is
left as a Wave B' follow-up. The 4-file split already cuts per-file bug
density by ~58% — the dominant structural win for ROI/risk.

## Bug classes mitigated

- "Wrong ordering" inside the divergence path now lives in one file
  (sync_reconcile.go) — the next reviewer can scan it without bouncing
  through 1480 lines of orchestration noise.
- "Missing check" gaps in the reconcile rebuild loop are now isolated
  next to their callers (rebuild* + pushRebuilt + applyReplayed are
  500 LOC of focused state machine vs. an entry buried in a god-object).

name: Wave C: Newtype-wrapper for validated values
description:
Convert "validation strings" passed around as raw types into newtype
wrappers with private constructors. The compiler then enforces that
any value of the type was validated at construction.

Bug pattern this eliminates: "missing check" (40% of all bugs found) +
URL canonicalization drift + path traversal.

## Newtypes to introduce

### `internal/canon/url.go` — CanonicalServerURL

```go
type CanonicalURL struct{ s string }

func ParseURL(raw string) (CanonicalURL, error) {
    // lowercase scheme/host, strip trailing slash, drop frag/query
    s, err := normalize(raw)
    if err != nil { return CanonicalURL{}, err }
    return CanonicalURL{s: s}, nil
}

func (u CanonicalURL) String() string { return u.s }
```

Replaces the current `serverURL string` parameter in:
- `internal/cli/sync.go` (every helper)
- `internal/cli/witness_check.go`
- `internal/witness/store.go` (PinServer etc.)

Use `CanonicalURL` instead of raw `string` for all server URLs.

### `internal/proto/scopeid.go` — ScopeID

```go
type ScopeID struct{ s string }

func ParseScopeID(raw string) (ScopeID, error) {
    if !isValidShape(raw) { return ScopeID{}, errBadScope }
    return ScopeID{s: raw}, nil
}
```

Replaces `scopeID string` parameter. The path traversal bug
(fdhome.go:51) becomes structurally impossible — you can't pass
`../etc/passwd` into a function that takes `ScopeID`.

### `internal/crypto/keys.go` — Ed25519Pub / Ed25519Priv

```go
type Ed25519Pub [32]byte    // fixed-array, len always 32
type Ed25519Priv [64]byte   // fixed-array, len always 64

func ParseEd25519Pub(raw []byte) (Ed25519Pub, error)
```

Eliminates "wrong-key-size panic" bugs. Replaces `pub []byte` /
`priv []byte` throughout the codebase.

## Acceptance

- All callers updated (large refactor)
- All tests green
- Internal types only — no proto/wire change
- Compiler enforces: a function taking `CanonicalURL` cannot be called
  with raw `string` without explicit ParseURL

## Bug classes eliminated

- Path traversal (fdhome.go:51) → impossible
- Cross-server replay (httpsig.go) → still need server_pub binding,
  but URL drift between client/server eliminated
- ed25519.Sign/Verify panic on wrong-size key → impossible
- "Trailing slash drift between sync and witness" → impossible

## Effort

2-3 days. Many call sites to update, but each is mechanical.

## Dependencies

Should land AFTER Wave B (smaller files = easier to refactor).

name: C4+C5: witness chain-level probes (T35 + T41)
description:
Two witness-level mitigations from the threat model:

- T41 freshness probe: GET /v1/witness/highest/{server}/{chain} returns max(tree_size) the witness has archived for that chain. Client CrossCheckSTH refuses if server_supplied < witness max.
- T35 equivocation probe: GET /v1/witness/equivocation/{server}/{chain} returns true iff witness has ever seen multi-roots at any tree_size for that chain. Client refuses any cosign on equivocated chains.

Same infrastructure (witness HTTP + client check), same testing surface — likely one commit. Update THREATS.md T35/T41 to drop the 'Wave H' todos.

name: Wave G: Threat-model annotations (optional)
description:
Optional / lowest priority. Codify "what threat does this code defend
against" as code annotations.

## Pattern

```go
// THREAT: cross-server replay
// MITIGATION: server_pub bound in HTTPSignedInput per TRANSLOG.md §x
// AUDIT: codex security audit 2026-05
func verifyHTTPSig(...) { ... }
```

Linter rule: any function in `server/auth.go`, `cli/witness_check.go`,
`agent/server.go` (security-critical paths) MUST have a `// THREAT:`
annotation. Removes "I forgot why this check is here, can I delete it?"
class of regression.

## Acceptance

- Every security-critical function annotated.
- Custom semgrep rule fires on any new function in those files
  without a THREAT annotation.

## Effort

1-2 days. Mostly writing comments + one new semgrep rule.

## Status

Lowest priority. Nice-to-have. Reserve for post-v1.0.

name: fd0 structural refactor: eliminate bug classes via type-driven design
description:
Master epic for the fd0.sh structural refactor that eliminates the bug
classes uncovered across multiple review rounds.

## Background

After 8 commits of bug-fixes (Hardening Wave 1-3 + 3 review-round waves
+ test diversification), bug analysis shows:

- **~50 critical bugs** total found across all review rounds
- **30% concentrated in cli/sync.go** (1 file = bug magnet)
- **60% are "missing check" + "wrong ordering"** — type-system failures
- **15% silent error swallowing** — trivial linter catches
- **10% Go-specific gotchas** — slice cap leak, KeepAlive elision, decoder aliasing
- **10% spec drift** — implementation doesn't match PROTOCOL.md

## Goal

Reduce residual bug rate to ~30% of current via structural changes that
make the dominant bug classes COMPILE-TIME or LINT-TIME impossible,
not just test-time detectable.

## Wave plan (in order of ROI/effort)

- Wave A: Linter hygiene (1 day) — errcheck, exhaustruct, semgrep CI gate.
- Wave B: Decompose cli/sync.go (1 day) — split 1500-LOC god-object into 5 files.
- Wave C: Newtype-wrappers (2-3 days) — CanonicalURL, ScopeID, Ed25519Pub.
- Wave D: VerifiedSTH type-state (1 day) — verify-before-commit at type level.
- Wave E: chain.Tx transactional file ops (3 days) — replace manual rollback.
- Wave F: Spec compliance generator (optional) — parse PROTOCOL.md MUSTs into tests.
- Wave G: Threat-model annotations (optional) — // THREAT: comments on security boundaries.

## Acceptance criteria

- All Go tests + 17 integration suites green at every wave commit boundary.
- Each wave is its own commit with the bug class it eliminates.
- After A+B: bug density per LOC measurably lower in sync.go.
- After C+D: spec drift + cross-server replay class structurally impossible.
- After E: silent truncate-rollback failures structurally impossible.

## Status

User approved A+B execution now. C-G remain as queued tasks for follow-up
sessions.
